title: The catering company's new contact wants 'the usual on the white van' and an answer about the price
purpose: Story S1, design rule R13 (resolved). Erin Castillo has just taken over the vans. She asks for 'the usual on the white van' and why it costs more. It takes Travis two questions to learn which van and what job. He books it, and answers the price with 'everything's gone up'. The account's visits fall from here.

mentioned.name: Bobby Shadden
mentioned.role: the fleet contact until the price rise

call.day: the Tuesday of week T-20 (rule R6; card S01, call 21)

scenario.who_calls: Erin Castillo, operations coordinator of company account A6, the fleet contact since the day of the price rise; she has a sheet her predecessor left.
scenario.vehicle: unit SC-2, a 2020 Ford Transit-250, BRC-2362 (accounts.json en.A6 fleet)
scenario.job: fleet PM service A: oil and filter, chassis lube, 50-point inspection
scenario.wants: 'the usual' booked, and to know why it is 270 on the website when her sheet says 255
scenario.what_happens: Travis asks which van; she says 'the big one'. He asks for the unit number on the key tag; it is SC-2. He names what was done last time and she confirms from her sheet. He says the price went up, answers her budget with 'everything's gone up', gives the out-the-door figure and a time, takes her number and books Thursday at 7:30.

unclear.kind: vague: 'the usual on the white van'
unclear.how: First question: which van (several are white). Second: the unit number on the key tag, and then what was done last time, which she confirms from her predecessor's sheet.

facts.note: A6 is a medium account and pays list. catalogue.json fleet_pm_van, class van, standard parts: 270.59 at today's hour and 255.59 at the hour before the rise (1.5 hours, so the rise is 15.00). Out the door with shop supplies 10.12 and sales tax: 306.68. He says 'two-seventy', 'two fifty-five' and 'three-oh-six and change'.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Travis.
Hi, Travis. This is Erin Castillo, I'm with Sourwood Catering? I've taken over the vans from Bobby Shadden.
Oh, okay! Yeah, Bobby told me he was handing those off. Nice to meet you, Erin. What do you need?
So I need to get the usual done on the white van. And I need somebody to explain to me why it costs more than it did last time.
Okay. We can do both. Which van are we talking about? Y'all have got about five white ones.
Um. The big one? Bobby just calls it the white van on his sheet.
That sounds like Bobby. Is there a unit number on the key tag, or can you read me the plate?
Hang on. ...It says S-C-two on the key.

S-C-two. Okay, that's the twenty-twenty Transit. And when you say the usual — last time that one was in, we did the P-M service. Oil and filter, grease the chassis, and the fifty-point inspection. Is that what Bobby's got written down?
Uh-huh.
It just says 'usual, two fifty-five.' That's my whole problem. I looked on your website and it says two-seventy.
Okay. So that's the P-M, and yeah, it's two-seventy now. It was two fifty-five.
Right.
Since when?
It just went up. First time we've raised the labor rate in better than two years.
Bobby didn't say anything about prices going up. I've got a budget he gave me, and it's got two fifty-five on every line.
Yeah, I hear you. Everything's gone up, Erin — parts, insurance, all of it — and we held that rate as long as we could. It's still a fair price for what you're getting.
Okay. I guess that's what it is.

So — out the door, with shop supplies and tax, that P-M's three-oh-six and change. Anything the inspection turns up, I call you before we touch it. And I can take S-C-two Thursday morning at seven-thirty and have it back to you by ten.
Okay.
Thursday... yeah. Thursday's okay, it doesn't go out till lunch.
Good. What's the best number for you? I've still got Bobby's on the account.
Four two three, five five five, oh one oh six.
Got it. Alright, Erin, I've got S-C-two down for Thursday at seven-thirty, and I'll write it up myself.
Okay. Do I need to do anything?
Just get it here. So that's Thursday, seven-thirty, P-M service on S-C-two, back by ten.
Okay. Thanks.
Thank you, Erin. Tell Bobby I said hey.
